articles.title: 12 Years Ago, 'Doctor Who's Most Unhinged Episode Revealed the Doctor at His Worst
articles.excerpt: Peter Capaldi's Twelfth Doctor has plenty of outstanding moments, but one episode in particular shows the Time Lord at his worst.
articles.body: Doctor Who has never shied away from showing the Doctor at his worst . In “A Good Man Goes to War,” Eleven (Matt Smith) realizes that his choices have made him nearly as monstrous as his enemies. In “The Waters of Mars,” Ten (David Tennant) is still reeling from the loss of his most recent companion, Donna Noble (Catherine Tate), and determined to win for once. He uses his power over time to save people whose deaths are fixed points in history, consequences be damned. It’s a genuinely shocking, villainous moment for the Time Lord.
articles.author: Aimee Hart

articles.title: PS4 Pro Belize DDR3 patch v2
articles.excerpt: The last time the DDR3 memory on PS4 pro has a critical problem it was capped under 11mb/s speed how much I tied I failed every time then I notice something while debugging through the southbridge wel…
articles.body: The last time the DDR3 memory on PS4 pro has a critical problem it was capped under 11mb/s speed how much I tied I failed every time then I notice something while debugging through the southbridge well it turns out DDR3 has it's own southbridge DMA engine but I don't really notice at first. and after some more debugging it turns out my DDR3 chip (1 GB on the southbridge) was being read by the CPU personally, 8 bytes at a time, through a tiny PCI window ~10.6 MB/s. and that was the main bottleneck of all. now it feels like I almost fix the issue but nope the southbridge DMA engine has no Linux driver for PS4 to use it. and after more debugging it turns out Sony's PS4 gameOS aka orbis uses that chip (their sbram driver), but the code is closed.
articles.author: Debarshi(Deb).S

After saving the same three PNGs all three ways: Pillow and plain sharp leave identical pixels, and the mozjpeg: true flag gave smaller files with fewer stray background pixels at the same quality. None of them gets the background to 100% pure 255. Unless I say otherwise the numbers below are means over three photos on one Apple M4 Mac, with Pillow 11.3.0 and sharp 0.34.5. KB here means 1024 bytes. What I fed them The photos are three shots from Wikimedia Commons, not mine: a teddy bear on a blue knit blanket, a Bohemian glass against a grey wall, and a pair of white sneakers on beige tile. All three are CC BY-SA 4.0, with credits under the chart.

articles.title: Handle Telegram Callback Queries in PHP Without Truncating Inline Keyboard Payloads
articles.excerpt: Interactive Telegram bots rely heavily on inline keyboards to guide users through multi-step workflows like order management, support ticket routing, or lead assignments. However, naive implementation…
articles.body: Interactive Telegram bots rely heavily on inline keyboards to guide users through multi-step workflows like order management, support ticket routing, or lead assignments. However, naive implementations of InlineKeyboardMarkup quickly break in production due to subtle constraints in the Telegram Bot API. The most frequent issue is the 64-byte limit on the callback_data parameter. If you attempt to serialize JSON objects, full UUIDs, or verbose action strings into a button's callback_data , Telegram silently drops the keyboard generation or throws an API error. Furthermore, if your backend fails to execute answerCallbackQuery immediately upon receiving a click, the mobile or desktop client keeps showing an endless loading spinner on the button until the interaction times out.

articles.title: Where did the 254s go? A heatmap of non-255 pixels in a white JPEG
articles.excerpt: A white sneaker photo, cut out and flattened onto white, is exactly 255 in the PNG. Save it as a JPEG at quality 85 and it isn't any more. A percentage tells me how much drifted, but when a rule says…
articles.body: A white sneaker photo, cut out and flattened onto white, is exactly 255 in the PNG. Save it as a JPEG at quality 85 and it isn't any more. A percentage tells me how much drifted, but when a rule says "pure white" I want to know where, so I built a heatmap. On this one photo, 10,403 pixels that were exactly 255 in the PNG no longer were after the JPEG, and the map puts them along the outline of the shoes. The photo is a Wikimedia Commons shot of white sneakers on beige tile (JustinLiang522, CC BY-SA 4.0). I made the white PNG in ImgIng ( https://imging.ai/ ), a browser-based image tool, in desktop Chromium: cutout, background set to white in the refine step, exported at 1,280×1,707.
articles.author: hao jia

articles.body: Your AI coding agent can read your .ssh folder. It can edit your hosts file. It can delete your whole C: drive if it goes wrong. Why are you letting it? The fix Map the agents workspace to its own drive letter. Done. Local folder workspaces: subst.scsoi.com WebDAV/cloud workspaces: drive.scsoi.com The agent sees a normal drive. articles.title: Your scraper's filter did nothing, and the run looked perfect
articles.excerpt: A scraper with a mode switch — dataType, chartType, scrapeType, whatever you call it — almost always has input fields that only make sense in some of those modes. Apple Podcasts's Actor is a clean exa…
articles.body: A scraper with a mode switch — dataType , chartType , scrapeType , whatever you call it — almost always has input fields that only make sense in some of those modes. Apple Podcasts 's Actor is a clean example: set dataType to reviews and you get keyword , minRating , maxRating , sort ; set it to episodes and you get minDurationSeconds , explicitFilter , a release-date window. Both sets live in the same input_schema.json , because the Actor handles both modes. That's normal, and it's also exactly the shape that produces this bug. The run that filtered nothing and said nothing We passed keyword: "AI" alongside dataType: "episodes" . keyword is a reviews-only field — the schema's own description says "Reviews only" — so the episodes code path never reads it.

articles.body: When Robert Altman's M*A*S*H arrived in theaters in 1970, its irreverent approach to the Korean War was unlike anything audiences had seen before. articles.body: SpaceX launched its newest batch of Starlink broadband internet satellites today (Oct. 23) from the California coast. The spacecraft, Starlink Group 15-15, were stacked 27 high inside the payload fairing of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket , which lifted off from Pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base at 6:48 p.m. EDT (2248 GMT; 3:48 p.m. local time in California). The rocket's first stage booster, designated B1063, executed its main engine cutoff and stage separation about 2.5 minutes into flight, sending the second stage to continue onward to low Earth orbit (LEO). articles.title: NASA’s Artemis III Mission to Test Future Moon Lander Operations
articles.excerpt: Before astronauts return to the lunar surface, NASA will first conduct one of the most ambitious and complex test missions in the agency’s history. Launching in 2027, Artemis III will send NASA astron…
articles.body: Before astronauts return to the lunar surface, NASA will first conduct one of the most ambitious and complex test missions in the agency’s history.  Launching in 2027, Artemis III will send NASA astronauts Randy Bresnik, Frank Rubio, Andre Douglas, and ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano aboard the Orion spacecraft into low Earth orbit to perform a series of demonstrations with test versions, or test articles, of human landing systems being developed by industry partners Blue Origin and SpaceX. During the planned 14-day mission, crews and flight controllers will practice the rendezvous, docking, habitation, and operational procedures that will be essential when Artemis astronauts begin landing near the Moon’s South Pole in 2028.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 23, 2007: NASA launches Harmony module to ISS on STS-120 space shuttle mission
articles.excerpt: On October 23, 2007, the space shuttle Discovery launched the Harmony module to the International Space Station. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On October 23, 2007, the space shuttle Discovery launched the Harmony module to the International Space Station . The Harmony module is a utility hub 14 feet wide and 24 feet long, or about the length of a minibus. It joins the European Space Agency's Columbus module and Japan's Kibo laboratory and serves as the crew quarters for the American astronauts. Once it was installed, the space station grew from about the size of a three-bedroom house to something more like a five-bedroom house. When astronauts delivered Harmony to the space station , they left it temporarily attached to the Unity node. After the shuttle left, astronauts used the space station's robotic arm to move the shuttle docking port out of the way at the Destiny module.
